title: Writing algebraic expressions
subtitle: Use a letter for a number you do not know yet. Then follow what happens to it.

explanation.title: A letter can take the place of a number
paragraphs: A game screen usually shows a number beside the coin symbol.
Sometimes you do not know that number yet.
A letter can take its place on the counter.
If the counter shows c, then c stands for the whole number of coins you started with.
If you win 200 more coins, the counter changes from c to c + 200.
key_points: The letter stands for the starting number.
A number beside a letter means multiply. For example, 3p means 3 × p.

steps.title: Start
steps.text: Write the letter that stands for the starting number.

steps.title: Follow
steps.text: Follow each change in the order it happens.

interactive.title: Build the expression
interactive.intro: Start with the letter. Choose each change in the story. Watch the expression grow one step at a time.

worked_examples.title: You win more coins
steps: Your coin counter starts at c.

worked_examples.title: Miguel, Adam and Josh
steps: Adam has twice as many songs, so Adam has 2p.
Josh has 30 more songs than Adam.

worked_examples.title: Two more wins
steps: A team starts with t points.

worked_examples.title: Triple your score, then collect a bonus
steps: A power-up triples your score, so it becomes 3s.

question_bank.title: Write the expression
question_bank.intro: Use stories about games, football, food and money. Start with the letter, then follow each change.
